issue.title: sase-core Rust 1.100 Clippy rejects four needless_bool guards
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-1t0.1 note #1 while implementing dangling artifact retention. Rust 1.100.0 Clippy rejects four old boolean-return guards under -D warnings:

- crates/sase_core/src/plan/decisions/grammar.rs:900-907 (valid_memory_selector)
- crates/sase_core/src/prompt_prediction/tokenize.rs:514-523
- crates/sase_core/src/prompt_prediction/tokenize.rs:838-844 (is_secret_like)
- crates/sase_core/src/tool_run/store/demand.rs:47-50 (valid_grant)

Evidence: feature-tree check 79adfed2e211f2b94150c4916418530f and clean-base check e9090c09c67111234aa63f4af9ef5a31 both failed exit 101 on these same four needless_bool denies. The clean run fingerprint has HEAD f28ce79ae806eca79cfe7f38d12451bbcba5fa61 and no dirty paths before or after. Its rustc/cargo versions are 1.100.0. Retained diagnostic snapshot: file:explicit:b4045c72067f344a59543fd3.

Landing audit at core 2159438daaad1b2925acde6a9a6dabfd3e79bca5 independently verified all three files are byte-identical to that clean base. Blame dates are 2026-10-08 for grammar and 2026-09-29/30 for prediction/demand, before this epic. No new compiler run was needed to corroborate the retained clean-base failure and unchanged source.

Scope: replace the four terminal if/return-literal sequences with their equivalent boolean expressions, preserving early checks and behavior. Follow sase-core AGENTS.md, run its wrapped sase tool run check, and retain the final result. This is small: the compiler supplies each exact expression, in three files, with no architecture or schema change.

Duplicate triage: all-status CI and all-type searches plus the last-week task sweep found no needless_bool report. Closed sase-1an covered different Rust 1.95 manual_range_contains/nonminimal_bool nodes; it was verified fixed on Rust 1.99 and should stay closed. Active epic scopes and sase-1hi/.1 notes were reviewed: this is newly exposed stable-toolchain lint compatibility across long-standing unrelated domains, not a regression from current Plan Decisions landing work. Link that epic for shared-file coordination; the current artifact-retention epic changes none of these expressions.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Both feature ToolRun 79adfed2e211f2b94150c4916418530f and clean-base ToolRun e9090c09c67111234aa63f4af9ef5a31 fail identically; the four flagged expressions remain unchanged at core 2159438d.
